newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FOCUS-Nestle slips despite profit gain.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Nestle slips despite profit gain.

text.p: International foods and beverage giant Nestle SA said net profit rose 20 percent in the first half of 1996 from the year-before period to 1.35 billion Swiss francs ($1.1 billion).
But its shares slid as dealers seized on its comment that it could not maintain such robust growth over the full year.
"The numbers were good, and the 20 percent growth is very good," one dealer in Zurich said. "But the trading margin went down and they said profit growth would slow," he added.
Sales pressure was coming primarily from British investors, he said.
Shares opened at 1,417 Swiss francs, down from the previous close at 1,423, and slipped to around 1,402 by mid-morning.
Nestle forecast favourable growth in sales and profit for the full year, but cautioned that net profit would not grow as fast in the second half as in the first six months.
The result nearly matched a consensus forecast among analysts for net profit of 1.36 billion Swiss francs.
Nestle said first half sales rose 5.6 percent to 28.44 billion Swiss francs, boosted primarily by internal sales growth. Currency fluctuations had a slight negative effect on turnover.

"For the full year 1996, Nestle expects the favourable trend in sales to continue, and consolidated sales for the year should approach 60 billion Swiss francs," it said in an interim report. 1995 sales totalled 56.48 billion Swiss francs.
Nestle said net profits would not rise as fast in the second half because the first half rate was based in part on comparison with a weak start to 1995.

"The net profit growth rate registered during the first six months of the year will not be sustained over the second semester, as its very favourable evolution is due to the comparison with a rather weak period during the first six months of 1995," it explained.
"For the whole of 1996, net profit should grow at least at the same rate as consolidated sales," it said. It did not give a precise estimate for 1996 profit.
Nestle posted a 1995 group net profit of 2.92 billion francs, down from 3.25 billion in 1994, when sales of cosmetics businesses produced an exceptional gain.

Nestle said the cost of goods sold dipped as a percentage of sales in the first half, but this was offset by increased marketing expenses to boost the group's brands as well as higher restructuring and amortisation costs.
It said its trading margin, which measures trading profit against sales, stood at 8.6 percent, down from 9.1 percent in 1995.
